definitions: To force or oblige someone to do something in the future.
To exert a strong, irresistible influence on someone to act in a certain way in the future.
examples: The new law will compel all citizens to register.
His conscience will compel him to confess.
Economic necessity will compel them to make changes.
pastTenses: compelled (past simple), compelled (present perfect), compelled (past perfect)
